blurb: Join us for an upcoming webinar exploring how Digital Twins and machine learning are advancing real-time decision-making in additive manufacturing. NAMRC 53 Best Paper Award - Encore Presentation! This session will introduce a new Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework designed to improve process control and part quality in Directed Energy Deposition (DED) additive manufacturing. Key topics include: • Using deep neural networks to improve real-time process predictions • How simultaneous multi-step forecasting increases computational efficiency • Achieving precise melt pool temperature control for improved part quality • Reducing porosity defects through laser power regulation • Comparing MPC performance against traditional PID control methods • Incorporating uncertainty quantification for more reliable decision-making under changing conditions • Adapting to process drift through continual validation and learning The presentation will highlight how prediction, optimization, and adaptive control can work together to support the next generation of Digital Twin-enabled manufacturing systems. Whether you work in additive manufacturing, automation, controls, or digital manufacturing, this session will provide practical insight into emerging approaches for autonomous manufacturing systems. blurb: Join us for an upcoming webinar exploring how Digital Twins and machine learning are advancing real-time decision-making in additive manufacturing. NAMRC 53 Best Paper Award - Encore Presentation! This session will introduce a new Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework designed to improve process control and part quality in Directed Energy Deposition (DED) additive manufacturing. Key topics include: • Using deep neural networks to improve real-time process predictions • How simultaneous multi-step forecasting increases computational efficiency • Achieving precise melt pool temperature control for improved part quality • Reducing porosity defects through laser power regulation • Comparing MPC performance against traditional PID control methods • Incorporating uncertainty quantification for more reliable decision-making under changing conditions • Adapting to process drift through continual validation and learning The presentation will highlight how prediction, optimization, and adaptive control can work together to support the next generation of Digital Twin-enabled manufacturing systems. Whether you work in additive manufacturing, automation, controls, or digital manufacturing, this session will provide practical insight into emerging approaches for autonomous manufacturing systems. Register today
